column3: The Hebrew makes captivity the object of restoration; BSB describes restoring Jacob from captivity.
The Hebrew pictures forgiveness as bearing guilt.
The Hebrew pictures collecting all Your fury; BSB says withheld.
The Hebrew repeats generation and generation; BSB says all generations.
The Hebrew explicitly has You returning and reviving, while BSB expresses this as revive us again.
The Hebrew’s final clause directly tells them not to return to folly; BSB makes Him the subject not letting them return.
The Hebrew names glory without the explicit His added by BSB.
The Hebrew has an uncompleted sprouting verb and a completed looking-down verb; BSB uses present verbs for both.
The Hebrew says set His steps on a way, without an explicit purpose clause of preparing a way as in BSB.
